D000298.s: Adolescent hospitalized for short term care.

D000566.s: The elaboration of dental enamel by ameloblasts, beginning with its participation in the formation of the dentino-enamel junction to the production of the matrix for the enamel prisms and interprismatic substance. (Jablonski, Dictionary of Dentistry, 1992).

D002487.s: An agency of the united states public health service that conducts and supports programs for the prevention and control of disease and provides consultation and assistance to health departments and other countries.

D002533.s: Radiography of the vascular system of the brain after injection of a contrast medium.

D003417.s: The branch of psychology which investigates the psychology of crime with particular reference to the personality factors of the criminal.

D004683.s: A group of alphavirus infections which affect horses and man, transmitted via the bites of mosquitoes. Disorders in this category are endemic to regions of South America and North America.

D005059.s: An exaggerated feeling of physical and emotional well-being not consonant with apparent stimuli or events; usually of psychologic origin, but also seen in organic brain disease and toxic states.

D005929.s: An idiopathic disorder of the tongue characterized by the loss of filiform papillae leaving reddened areas of circinate macules bound by a white band. The lesions heal, then others erupt.

D006335.s: General or unspecified injuries to the heart.

D006340.s: The heart rate of the fetus. The normal range at term is between 120 and 160 beats per minute.

D006551.s: Stomach herniation located at or near the diaphragmatic opening for the esophagus, the esophageal hiatus.

D006832.s: A congenital condition where the greater portions of the cerebral hemispheres and corpus striatum are replaced by CSF and glial tissue. The meninges and the skull are well formed, which is consistent with earlier normal embryogenesis of the telencephalon.

D009693.s: Widely used technique which exploits the ability of complementary sequences in single-stranded DNAs or RNAs to pair with each other to form a double helix.

D009767.s: The condition of weighing two, three, or more times the ideal weight, so called because it is associated with many serious and life-threatening disorders. In the body mass index, morbid obesity is defined as having a BMI greater than 40.0 kg/m2.

D009833.s: Set of nerve fibers conducting impulses from olfactory receptors to the cerebral cortex. It includes the olfactory nerve; olfactory bulb; olfactory tract; olfactory tubercle; anterior perforated substance; and olfactory cortex.

D010026.s: An abnormal hardening or increased density of bone tissue.

D010260.s: A personality disorder characterized by the avoidance of accepting deserved blame and an unwarranted view of others as malevolent. The latter is expressed as suspiciousness, hypersensitivity, and mistrust.

D010808.s: Systematic and thorough inspection of the patient for physical signs of disease or abnormality.

D010901.s: Examinations that evaluate functions of the pituitary gland.

D010996.s: Presence of fluid in the pleural cavity resulting from excessive transudation or exudation from the pleural surfaces. It is a sign of disease and not a diagnosis in itself.

D011209.s: The exertion of a strong influence or control over others in a variety of settings--administrative, social, academic, etc.

D011872.s: Hospital department which is responsible for the administration and provision of x-ray diagnostic and therapeutic services.

D013614.s: Abnormally rapid heartbeats with sudden onset and cessation.

D013823.s: Cellular receptors which mediate the sense of temperature. Thermoreceptors in vertebrates are mostly located under the skin. In mammals there are separate types of thermoreceptors for cold and for warmth and nociceptors which detect cold or heat extreme enough to cause pain.

D014163.s: Change in learning in one situation due to prior learning in another situation. The transfer can be positive (with second learning improved by first) or negative (where the reverse holds).

D014361.s: Serine proteinase inhibitors which inhibit trypsin. They may be endogenous or exogenous compounds.

D014695.s: Radiography of the ventricular system of the brain after injection of air or other contrast medium directly into the cerebral ventricles. It is used also for x-ray computed tomography of the cerebral ventricles.

D015205.s: The geographic area of the northwestern region of the United States. The states usually included in this region are Idaho, Montana, Oregon, Washington, and Wyoming.

D015270.s: A nontuberculous infection when occurring in humans. It is characterized by pulmonary disease, lymphadenitis in children, and systemic disease in AIDS patients. Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare infection of birds and swine results in tuberculosis.

D015436.s: Inflammation of the underlying layer of adipose tissue (panniculus) of the peritoneum, usually of the mesentery or the omentum. There are several forms with various names and are usually characterized by infiltration of lymphocytes and neutrophils, fat necrosis, and fibrosis.

D016118.s: A strong ligament of the knee that originates from the posteromedial portion of the lateral condyle of the femur, passes anteriorly and inferiorly between the condyles, and attaches to the depression in front of the intercondylar eminence of the tibia.

D016420.s: Work consisting of a critical or explanatory note written to discuss, support, or dispute an article or other presentation previously published. It may take the form of an article, letter, editorial, etc.

D016903.s: The process of observing, recording, or detecting the effects of a chemical substance administered to an individual therapeutically or diagnostically.

D017276.s: Surface resistance to the relative motion of one body against the rubbing, sliding, rolling, or flowing of another with which it is in contact.

D017760.s: Displacement of bones out of line in relation to joints. It may be congenital or traumatic in origin.

D018174.s: Infections caused by viruses of the genus arterivirus.

D018303.s: Rare indolent tumors comprised of neoplastic glial and neuronal cells which occur primarily in children and young adults. Benign lesions tend to be associated with long survival unless the tumor degenerates into a histologically malignant form.

D018497.s: A condition in which the right ventricle of the heart was functionally impaired. This condition usually leads to heart failure or myocardial infarction, and other cardiovascular complications.

D019065.s: The assembly of viral structural proteins and nucleic acid (viral dna or viral rna) to form a virus particle.

D019296.s: Continuous recording of the carbon dioxide content of expired air.

D019458.s: Generally refers to the amount of protection available and the kind of loss which would be paid for under an insurance contract with an insurer. (Slee & Slee, Health Care Terms, 2d ed)

D019599.s: Axons of certain cells in the dentate gyrus. They project to the polymorphic layer of the dentate gyrus and to the proximal dendrites of pyramidal cells of the hippocampus. These mossy fibers should not be confused with mossy fibers that are cerebellar afferents (see nerve fibers).

D019960.s: Excretory-related psychiatric disorders usually diagnosed in infancy or childhood.

D020029.s: Pairing of purine and pyrimidine bases by hydrogen bonding in double-stranded DNA or RNA.

D020656.s: A transitional diencephalic zone of the thalamus consisting of complex and varied cells lying caudal to the ventral posterolateral nucleus, medial to the rostral part of the pulvinar, and dorsal to the medial geniculate body.

D038301.s: Inactivation of viruses by non-immune related techniques. They include extremes of pH, HEAT treatment, ultraviolet radiation, ionizing radiation; desiccation; antiseptics; disinfectants; organic solvents, and detergents.

D041622.s: Projection of near-IR light (infrared rays), in the 700-1000 nm region, across an object in parallel beams to an array of sensitive photodetectors. This is repeated at various angles and a mathematical reconstruction provides three dimensional medical imaging of tissues.

D042241.s: Methods to determine in patients the nature of a disease or disorder at its early stage of progression. Generally, early diagnosis improves prognosis and treatment outcome.

D048690.s: The fruiting 'heads' or 'caps' of fungi, which as a food item are familiarly known as mushrooms, that contain the fungal spores.

D056424.s: Excision of part of the skull. This procedure is used to treat elevated intracranial pressure that is unresponsive to conventional treatment.

D058567.s: Chemical compound used to initiate polymerization of dental resins by the use of dental curing lights. It absorbs UV light and undergoes decomposition into free radicals that initiate polymerization process of the resins in the mix.

D060205.s: Methods used to temporarily or permanently block the flow of body fluids through various ducts and tubules throughout the body, including blood vessels and lymphatic vessels such as by therapeutic embolization or ligation.

D060436.s: A naturally occurring reproductive phenomenon of flowering plants where self-incompatibility arises due to differences between nucleus, cytoplasm, mitochondria, or chloroplasts that occur in gamete cells from separate sources when they are brought together by cross-hybridization or in vitro…

D061228.s: Traumatic injuries to the hypoglossal nerve.

D062526.s: The process of helping patients to effectively and efficiently use the health care system when faced with one or more of these challenges: (1) choosing, understanding, and using health coverage or applying for assistance when uninsured; (2) choosing, using, and understanding different types of…

D064872.s: Small sets of evidence-based interventions for a defined patient population and care setting.

D065808.s: A neurophysiological phenomenon in which the response to a startling stimulus (pulse) is decreased when a weaker prestimulus (prepulse) precedes it closely in time. It is used as an operational measure of sensorimotor gating.

D000076042.s: A neurological disorder characterized by inattentiveness and the inability to form short term memories. It is caused by thiamine deficiency due to chronic alcoholism.

D000077711.s: Profound inattention by individuals to their own health and hygiene.

D000078602.s: Feeling or showing sorrow; the sense of being unhappy. It is related to depression but is not synonymous.

D000089062.s: Institutional and personal security measures designed to prevent the loss, theft, misuse, diversion or intentional release of pathogens and toxins.(from https://www.who.int/influenza/pip/BiosecurityandBiosafety_EN_20Mar2018.pdf February,24, 2021)

D000091702.s: Interconnections of social categorizations such as race, class, and gender, creating overlapping and interdependent systems of discrimination or disadvantage.

D000092682.s: Technological process of recording the motion and movement of objects (e.g., surgical instrument in robotic surgery), body parts (e.g., eye movement), animals or people.

D000095463.s: Printed image made using photographic images.
